The likely fault is in [load_book.py](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/load_book.py:138). `find_author` stops at the first nonempty name query before `find_entity` checks dates, and its surname query compares full date strings. That can prevent a valid fallback match between authors whose dates share years but use different formats. Input `*` characters also reach wildcard queries unescaped.

[remove_author_honorifics](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/load_book.py:222) takes a dictionary instead of a string, matches prefixes without a word boundary, and can turn an honorific-only name into an empty name. New-author creation copies only selected fields. [extract_year](/app/openlibrary/core/helpers.py:330) already extracts the first four-digit run, but matching does not use it.

The fix should check extracted birth and death years at each match stage, attempt surname matching only with both valid input years, treat input asterisks literally, and preserve all fields when creating an author. Query escaping needs verification against both Infobase and its mock. The 113 existing focused tests pass; they do not cover the reported cases. Per this checkout’s fault-localization scope, I changed no project source or tests.

Updated author matching in [load_book.py](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/load_book.py). It now checks extracted years at each name-match stage, uses surname matching only when both input years are valid, and treats asterisks in names literally. Honorific removal accepts a string and handles exceptions and honorific-only names. New author records retain the input fields.

Updated the query mock and added regression tests. The focused suite passed: **180 passed, 1 expected failure**.

VERDICT: FIX

The patch has two matching defects in [load_book.py](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/load_book.py:137):

- An exact name returns no match when the input has no birth date but the stored author does. A local reproduction returned `None` for “Jane Writer” with a stored birth year of 1902. Compare extracted years when both records provide the date.
- For “Smith, John,” a flipped-name result with a lower key outranks the exact-name result. A local reproduction selected `John Smith` (`OL1A`) over `Smith, John` (`OL9A`). Resolve the exact-name tier before considering flipped names.

**Tests executed:** `pytest -q openlibrary/catalog/add_book/tests/test_load_book.py openlibrary/tests/core/test_helpers.py` — 54 passed; `pytest -q openlibrary/tests/catalog/test_utils.py` — 85 passed. These tests do not cover the reproduced cases. No test environment problem. I made no project code changes as required for this independent review.

Fixed both review findings: author matching now compares date years when both records provide them, and a match for the supplied name takes priority over a flipped-name match. Added regression tests for both cases.

The reviewer’s test commands pass: 56 tests in the load-book and helper suites, and 85 in the catalog utils suite. `git diff --check` also passes.
